q: For x(t) = 393 cos(2 pi 427 t) (1 ohm reference), the average power P is:
h: P = A^2 / 2 for any sinusoid, independent of frequency.
f: Step 1: identify amplitude A = 393. Step 2: P = A^2/2 = 154449/2 = 77224.5. Check: average of cos^2 over a period is 1/2, and frequency 427 Hz does not change the average.

q: Evaluate the integral over all t of (t^2 + 657) delta(t - (386)) dt:
h: Sifting: the impulse samples the bracket at t = t0.
f: Step 1: sifting property: integral of x(t) delta(t - t0) dt = x(t0). Step 2: x(386) = 386^2 + 657 = 149653. Check: everything away from t = 386 is multiplied by zero.

q: The system y[n] = x[n] + x[n - 920] is classified as: (spaced-repetition variant 3807)
o: With memory and noncausal
With memory, causal, linear and time-invariant
Memoryless and causal
Memoryless and noncausal
h: It uses the present sample and a past sample only.
f: Step 1: x[n - 920] is a past sample, so the system has memory. Step 2: no future samples appear, so it is causal. Step 3: it is a fixed linear combination with constant coefficients, hence linear and time-invariant.

q: Convolving x[n] = {143, 346} with h[n] = {797, 427} (both starting at n = 0), the value y[1] is:
X(s) = 1 / ((s + 144)(s + 445)) with causal ROC. In x(t), the coefficient multiplying e^(-144 t) is:
h: Cover-up: set s = -a in 1/(s + b).
f: Step 1: partial fractions: A/(s+144) + B/(s+445) with A = 1/(445 - 144) = 0.0033. Step 2: x(t) = (0.0033 e^(-144 t) - 0.0033 e^(-445 t)) u(t). Check: x(0+) = 0, matching the initial-value behaviour of this strictly proper X(s).

q: x[n] = (0.6461)^n u[n]. The sample x[3] is:
h: Cube the base; u[3] = 1.
f: Step 1: x[3] = (0.6461)^3. Step 2: = 0.2697. Check: |a| = 0.6461 is below 1, so the ROC |z| above 0.6461 includes the unit circle: decaying and stable.

q: An odd square wave of amplitude 94 has sine harmonics (4A/(k pi)) sin(k w0 t) for odd k. The amplitude of the k = 3 harmonic is:
h: Substitute k into 4A/(k pi).
f: Step 1: amplitude = 4 x 94 / (3 pi). Step 2: = 39.8948 (4 decimal places). Check: it falls as 1/k, so higher harmonics weaken - the origin of Gibbs ripple concentration near jumps.

q: A 2619 Hz tone is sampled at fs = 2677 Hz. It aliases to:
h: Fold: alias = |f - k fs| for the integer k giving a result in [0, fs/2].
f: Step 1: Nyquist needs fs at least 5238 Hz, so 2677 Hz undersamples. Step 2: alias = |2619 - 1 x 2677| = 58 Hz. Check: 58 lies in [0, 1338], the representable baseband.

q: Bandwidth B = 1523 kHz and SNR = 52 dB. The Shannon capacity is approximately (bps):
h: C = B log2(1 + SNR), with SNR converted from dB first.
f: Step 1: SNR linear = 10^(52/10) = 158489.319. Step 2: C = 1523000 x log2(1 + 158489.319) which is about 26308356 bps. Check: Shannon is an upper bound; a practical rate must stay below it, then Nyquist sets the levels.

q: AM with modulating bandwidth BWm = 24.7 kHz has total transmission bandwidth:
h: AM keeps both sidebands: BWt = 2 x BWm.
f: Step 1: sidebands sit at fc +/- up to 24.7 kHz. Step 2: BWt = 2 x 24.7 = 49.4 kHz. Check: SSB would need only 24.7 kHz, at the cost of sharper filtering.

q: A state matrix A has characteristic polynomial lambda^2 + (170) lambda + (5929). Its eigenvalues (the system poles) are:
h: Factor the quadratic: (lambda - r1)(lambda - r2).
f: Step 1: lambda^2 + (170) lambda + (5929) = (lambda - (-49))(lambda - (-121)). Step 2: eigenvalues are -49 and -121. Check: sum of roots = -170, product = 5929, matching trace and determinant relations.

q: Total energy of x(t) = e^(-424 t) u(t) (1 ohm reference) is: (spaced-repetition variant 3808)
h: E = integral of e^(-2a t) from 0 to infinity.
f: Step 1: square the signal: |x|^2 = e^(-848 t) for t at least 0. Step 2: E = 1/(2a) with a = 424, so E = 0.0012. Check: finite positive energy, so this is an energy signal with P = 0.

q: For y(t) = x(26 t - 17862), the time shift (after factoring) is:
h: Rewrite as x(a (t - b/a)) and read off the shift.
f: Step 1: 26 t - 17862 = 26 (t - 687). Step 2: compression by 26 with shift right by 687. Check: the common wrong answer is 17862, the unfactored constant.

q: The system y(t) = 63 x(t) + 951 is:
o: Nonlinear: zero input gives output 951, violating the zero-in zero-out rule
Linear: it is a straight-line graph
Memoryless, therefore linear
Time-varying but linear
h: Test x = 0 first; a linear system must answer 0.
f: Step 1: with x(t) = 0 the output is 951, not 0. Step 2: superposition fails, so the system is nonlinear (affine). Check: the term 63 x(t) alone would be linear; the offset 951 breaks it.

q: For x[n] = {86, 337} and h[n] = {852, 530}, the sum of all output samples (sum of y[n]) is:
h: Sum of a convolution = (sum of x) x (sum of h).
f: Step 1: sum of x = 423, sum of h = 1382. Step 2: product = 584586. Check: direct convolution gives y = {73272, 332704, 178610}, summing to 584586.

q: H(s) has denominator s^2 + (-35) s + (264), i.e. poles at s = 24 and s = 11. For the causal system:
o: Anticausal and stable for every ROC
Stable because the poles are real
Causal but unstable: a pole is not in the left-half plane
Unstable only if the zeros are in the right-half plane
h: Causal + stable needs every pole strictly in the left-half plane.
f: Step 1: poles are 24 and 11. Step 2: at least one pole is not negative, so the causal ROC excludes part or all of the jw axis: not BIBO stable. Check: zeros do not decide stability.

q: A causal discrete-time LTI system has a single pole at z = 0.822. It is:
o: Stable whenever the pole is real
Unstable only for complex poles
Causal and stable: pole inside the unit circle
Stable because the ROC is outside the pole
h: Causal + stable needs every pole strictly inside |z| = 1.
f: Step 1: |pole| = 0.822 is below 1. Step 2: the causal ROC outside the pole therefore includes the unit circle: stable.

q: A filter has peak magnitude response 791. At its 3-dB frequency the magnitude is: (spaced-repetition variant 3808)
h: 3-dB means half power, so magnitude scales by 1/sqrt(2).
f: Step 1: |H| at 3-dB = 791 / sqrt(2). Step 2: = 559.321. Check: (559.321)^2 is approximately half of 791^2 = 625681, confirming half power.
